attempts.summary: On node1 (Alpine Linux 3.23, busybox crond/crontab via bbsuid), restricted cron scheduling to root and opsadmin only. Since busybox crontab has no cron.allow/cron.deny support, implemented access control via a wrapper: moved the real crontab binary (symlink to /bin/bbsuid) into a root:cron-owned directory /usr/libexec/cron-real (mode 0710, blocking traversal by non-root/non-cron-group users), and replaced /usr/bin/crontab with a shell wrapper that checks the caller's username against an allowlist (root, opsadmin) before exec'ing the real binary. Created the opsadmin user with a locally generated random password, added opsadmin to the cron group, enabled and started the crond service (rc-update add crond default), and verified end-to-end: root and opsadmin can list/install/remove crontabs, the existing 'alpine' user is denied both via the wrapper and via direct-path bypass attempts. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured pre-restart boot_id and service health, issued a backgrounded `reboot` so the ack returned before disconnection, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed boot_id changed (446f0a24... -> ff186243...) with fresh uptime (~30s), and re-verified crond was running and the cron access control (wrapper file, directory permissions, allow/deny behavior for opsadmin vs alpine) was fully intact post-reboot.
